_about: Steve edits this file: all the wording in the avalanche danger panel. Words in {curly brackets} are filled in by the app; keep them, move them, or drop them. Placeholder wording until Steve rewrites it (brief, step 5 check-in).
heading: Avalanche danger
authority: From {source}, issued {issued}. Their forecast is the authority: read it in full before you go.
bandNote: This zone is mostly {band}, so that row is highlighted.
earlySeason: Early season: {source} isn't issuing daily danger ratings yet. Avalanches can happen wherever there's enough snow to slide.
expired: This forecast expired {when}. Check {source} for a newer one before you go.
saved: Couldn't refresh the forecast, so this is the copy saved on your device {age} ago.
unavailable: Couldn't load the avalanche forecast. Check {link} directly before you go.
noCentre: No avalanche centre forecasts this spot. Without a forecast, you're relying on your own observations and snowpack assessment.
overallNote: This is the highest danger anywhere in the {zone} forecast zone. Danger by elevation and the avalanche problems are in the full forecast.
problemNotInBand: Not forecast at this zone's elevation.
aspectMatch: This zone faces {aspect}, one of the aspects named for this problem.
caution: {danger} in this zone's elevation band on {day}. On days like this, simple, lower-angle and treed terrain is the lower-consequence choice. {steep}% of this zone is steeper than 30°.
cantSee: This app can't see buried weak layers, slab structure, cornices, glide cracks or local wind effects. The forecast and what you see on the day can.
notSafe: A low rating, or no rating, never means the terrain is safe.
